rationale: Round 7 — round 6 was VOIDED by bugs_open/019 (review_editquality truncated at max_tokens=8000, whole round discarded, no verdict; reproduction logged in the 019 case file), so this is the same plan resubmitted, not a revision. Substance, as of the round-5 guardian veto and its fixes: the veto was correct — the persistence call in handleCompleteResponse was unconditional, a fleet-wide ungoverned condition-reporting channel any future adapter could feed by emitting the key. This plan implements the guardian's contained alternative (a) verbatim: persistReportedConditions is GATED on response.Headers.Sender.AgentType against an explicit allowlist (conditionReportingAgentTypes = {"image-generator"}); non-sanctioned pipelines provably pay one map lookup and nothing else; an unsanctioned sender emitting the field is warned by name and never persisted. Alternative (b) (gate via agent_definitions.output_contract) was considered and rejected with stated reasons: config lookup in the fleet's hottest path, and the documented config re-seed clobber landmine would make the gate's ground truth mutable outside code review; senderMayReportConditions is the single swap seam if architecture review later prefers (b). Also fixed per bug_historian (round 5): parseReportedConditions returns a malformed flag — present-but-not-a-list and all-junk lists warn 'the reporting contract broke; conditions were lost, fix the emitter' instead of reading as healthy; empty list stays benign; test-pinned. editquality's residual check is answered by compilation: generateImage has exactly two return points, both on the 5-value signature, go build passes. The underlying problem is unchanged: the adapter's routing guards (UNROUTED KIND / bad hint / dropped anchors) die in pod logs — today's post-roll generations proved it when the routing decision's only witness was a log line on one of two replicas. Adapter stays DB-free; chassis never re-derives the routing table; the coupling is one field name plus one consumer-owned allowlist. The DECLARED CONTRACTS guideline gap stays a named side-task; this plan no longer depends on it — the gate makes the channel scoped-by-default.

plan.summary: The image adapter's routing guards (UNROUTED KIND, bad provider_hint, dropped reference anchors) currently die in pod logs. Add a pure reportedConditions() next to the routing table that turns routingDecision flags into condition records; thread them through generateImage into the success response body as `reported_conditions`; on the chassis, parseReportedConditions + persistReportedConditions in agent_error_log.go write each to agent_error_log (severity 'warning', resolved=false, sender identity from response headers), called once from handleCompleteResponse — reachable only after ProcessResponse's atomic claim (no duplicate persists), and now GATED on an explicit sender allowlist (guardian's round-5 contained alternative) so every non-sanctioned pipeline is provably untouched. Absent field = healthy case (one map lookup); present-but-malformed = loud contract-break warning, never a silent healthy-looking nil (bug_historian's round-5 catch); old chassis ignores the field, old adapter sends none, so the two images may roll separately.

plan.risks: 1) Hot path: for every non-sanctioned pipeline the call is now provably one map lookup (gate short-circuits before parse); for sanctioned senders, parse + best-effort inserts only when conditions exist. 2) The allowlist is a hand-maintained list IN THE CONSUMER — deliberate: it is an authorisation record, mismatches fail LOUD (named warning), and it does not predict another binary's config, so it is not the routing-table drift class; if architecture review later prefers declaring via output_contract, senderMayReportConditions is the single swap seam. 3) No dedup across responses: N unrouted generations = N rows (capped 10/response; per-response duplicates impossible via the atomic claim). Row count is the signal's size; rows group by error_code. 4) Contract-break behaviour: malformed field → conditions LOST for that response (warned, not persisted) — the alternative, persisting a synthetic 'malformed' row, was rejected as inventing data; the warn names the emitter to fix. 5) Split-roll safe both directions: old chassis ignores the field; old adapter sends none. 6) Best-effort semantics inherited from logAgentError. DEPLOY VERIFICATION COMMITMENT (unchanged from round 5): kubectl exec <each image-generator-adapter pod> -- sh -c 'strings /app/image-generator-adapter | grep -c "UNROUTED_IMAGE_KIND"' → 1 and 'grep -c "REFERENCE_ANCHORS_DROPPED"' → 1 (positive control: 'grep -c "UNROUTED KIND"' → 1); kubectl exec <each agent-chassis pod> -- sh -c 'strings /app/agent-chassis | grep -c "UNSANCTIONED sender"' → 1 and 'grep -c "Persisted adapter-reported conditions"' → 1; both replicas of both services. Then live-fire: one generation with a deliberately unrouted kind → SELECT error_code, severity, agent_type FROM agent_error_log WHERE error_code='UNROUTED_IMAGE_KIND' ORDER BY occurred_at DESC LIMIT 1. PROVENANCE WRITE-BACK: on landing, a doc_note records the contract, the gate, and the landing commit against diagnosis item 5db192c5 — which stays OPEN for the remaining drift-family members.
